newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends higher on Canada labor concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends higher on Canada labor concerns.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher in thin trade on short covering sparked by growing concerns over labor problems in Canada, although closing prices were off the day's highs, traders said.
Lumber closed $3.50 to $0.20 per thousand board feet higher with July up $2.40 at $371.60 per tbf and September up $2.40 at $366.70 per tbf.

Labor concerns developed when a strike date was announced by pulp and paper workers against Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd. A strike by that union may prompt union members working at other lumber firms to be more inclined to strike if negotiations with major lumber companies hit snags, traders said.
Strength in futures came despite a weak technical picture and a continued weak cash market, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $361 per tbf, off $1 from last Friday and $3 under the last midweek level. Demand for wood has been slower than expected since the holiday, they said.
